messages:
pagerbot: SEV2 ALERT — GPU pool 'eu-general-1' at 100% capacity, queue growth detected, throttling engaged. Auto-scale attempted and hit max limit. link: https://infra.redwood.internal/alerts/5101234567 :rotating_light:

arjun: acked. oncall running. seeing queue spike ~14k pending, throttle ratio 62% across pool. any recent rollouts?

maria: I pushed a config flip earlier at 10:12 UTC that tightened continuous batching window from 250ms -> 25ms for latency experiments (commit 7a9c3b2). rolled as canary to eu region only.

jen: hmm that would reduce batching — should reduce throughput but also change cache access patterns. getting logs now.

phil: grabbing metrics: 1m QPS up 3x for a small group, prefix_cache_hit dropped from 82% -> 5% in last 6m. KV cache eviction rate spiked.

sam: confirm: autoscaler responded but hit scale cap (pool max instances = 18). pool was already near cap due to longer running generative jobs earlier.

ops-liz: customer impact: some latency-sensitive customers report 5xx/timeout spikes. Support alerting on two enterprise tenants — likely throttled.

arjun: immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert the canary batching change (7a9c3b2) 2) increase pool cap temporarily + request manual node add 3) enable a soft-fallback routing to dedicated-reserved pool for affected tenants

maria: rolling back now — starting rollback job: `git revert -m 1 7a9c3b2 && deploy --region eu --tag rollback-mw-510123`

jen: while rollback is in flight, suggest re-enabling prefix cache warmup and bump TTL to reduce cold miss pressure. patch: `infractl cache update --pool eu-general-1 --prefix-warmup true --ttl 300s`

phil: applying warmup patch now. also throttling policy temporarily relaxed to allow higher concurrency (risk: higher memory).

sam: asked infra to add 3 gpus to pool as emergency: `rctl scale pool eu-general-1 +3 --reason "sev2 emergency"` — pending approval, should be live in ~90s once scheduler finishes.

ops-liz: notifying affected customers via status page and support channel. small tenants on shared tier may see degraded throughput until mitigations finish.

maria: rollback completed and verified (deploy tag rollback-mw-510123). snapshot: continuous batching window back to 250ms.

arjun: good. need to watch queue. current pending queue down from 14k -> 5.2k and falling. prefix_cache_hit rising to ~47% after warmup patch.

phil: autoscaler added +2 GPUs (manual bump) — still below recommended but helps throughput. eviction rate reduced by 70%.

sam: routing for two impacted enterprise tenants applied: traffic moved to reserved pool eu-enterprise-1, no customer timeouts observed there.

ops-liz: raising incident bridge for postmortem, capturing timeline. customers notified with ETA for full recovery ~30m.

arjun: next actions: 1) lock down canary rollout criteria (traffic/kv-cache impact) 2) add autoscale safety buffer so canary region can't exhaust pooled capacity 3) add metric alarm for prefix_cache_hit drop >20% over 5m 4) postmortem owner: maria

maria: agreed. I'll own the postmortem. creating doc: https://docs.internal/redwood/incident/5101234567

jen: quick note for SRE — investigate why warmup was disabled by default for that canary. add preflight for cache warmup state before batching changes roll out.

pagerbot: Incident: MITIGATED (partial) — queue decreasing, throttling reduced, rollback + warmup applied, manual scale + tenant reroute in progress. Pager handoff to next oncall in 2h for follow-up.

arjun: thanks all — keep monitoring dashboards (tokens: per-route, prefix_cache_hit, pending_queue). will update status page with final recovery once stable. :white_check_mark:
